title: Overdue and archived behaviour on shared tasks; frozen shares
description:
## What to build

Overdue marking and archiving behave on shared tasks exactly as on a user's own tasks.

In "Shared with me", overdue tasks are marked "Overdue" by the same rule. Archived tasks are hidden by default and appear, marked "Archived", when the recipient turns on "show archived". An archived task that was shared remains visible to its recipients in that archived view, and is read-only whatever their role: an edit recipient can change nothing.

An archived task rejects every mutation except deletion by its owner, and that includes sharing and revoking: its shares are frozen until the task is deleted. The owner's share panel on an archived task still lists the shares but offers no way to share, change a role or revoke.

Covers spec stories 44, 63, and the frozen-shares rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In "Shared with me", a not-done shared task with a due date before today is marked "Overdue"; one due today is not
- [ ] An edit recipient completing an overdue shared task removes the mark for both recipient and owner
- [ ] Shared tasks completed more than 30 days ago are hidden from the default "Shared with me" list
- [ ] "Show archived" on "Shared with me" lists them marked "Archived" and survives a reload
- [ ] An archived shared task shows no edit or status controls to a recipient with the edit role
- [ ] The server refuses a change to an archived task from an edit recipient, even from a stale page, and the task is unchanged
- [ ] On an archived task the owner sees the existing shares but cannot share, replace a role or revoke; the server refuses these even from a stale page
- [ ] The owner can delete an archived shared task, and it then disappears from the recipient's archived view

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database, clock set to 2030-03-10 12:00 UTC. Two independent browser sessions: A as `a@example.com`, B as `b@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`). As A create "Late task" (due 2030-03-09), "On time task" (due 2030-03-10) and "Finished task"; share all three with B with the edit role. As A mark "Finished task" done.

1. As B, open "Shared with me".
2. As B, mark "Late task" done. As A, reload "My tasks".
3. As B, open "Finished task" and leave its edit form open. As A, open "Finished task" and leave the share panel open in a second tab.
4. Set the clock to 2030-04-10 12:00 UTC (31 days after "Finished task" was completed).
5. As B, reload "Shared with me", then turn on "show archived" and reload again.
6. As B, open "Finished task" from the list.
7. As B, in the stale form from step 3, change the title to "Changed" and save.
8. As A, open "Finished task" fresh (with "show archived" on in "My tasks").
9. As A, in the stale tab from step 3, try to revoke `b@example.com`, then try to share again with the view role.
10. As A, delete "Finished task" and confirm. As B, reload "Shared with me" with "show archived" on.

**Expected:** in step 1 "Late task" is marked "Overdue" and "On time task" is not. After step 2 "Late task" is not marked overdue for B or A. After step 5 "Finished task" is absent from B's default list and present, marked "Archived", with "show archived" on (before and after reload). In step 6 B sees all fields, role edit, and no edit or status controls. Step 7 is refused with a message that archived tasks cannot be changed. In step 8 A sees `b@example.com` listed with role edit and no share form or revoke control. Both attempts in step 9 are refused with the same kind of message, and a reload shows B's share unchanged with role edit and the title still "Finished task". After step 10 "Finished task" is gone from B's list. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the refused actions in steps 7 and 9.

**Edge case:** as B (edit role) with the clock at 2030-04-10, "Late task" (completed 2030-03-10, exactly 31 days earlier) is also archived and read-only, while "On time task" (never completed) is still editable and is now marked "Overdue".

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.9 Overdue marking and overdue-only filter
- task-master-42j.10 Archived tasks: hidden, opt-in, read-only, owner can delete
- task-master-42j.12 Edit role, replacing a role, and server-side refusal
- task-master-42j.13 Revoke a share and delete cascade
close_reason: shared overdue/archived and frozen shares done

title: Revoke a share and delete cascade
description:
## What to build

An owner revokes a share from the task's share panel, ending that recipient's access. Access is checked on every request, so revoking takes effect on the recipient's next request, including on a page they already have open: the task vanishes from their "Shared with me" list and its address shows the same not-found page as a task that does not exist.

Deleting a task deletes its shares, so the task disappears from every recipient's list and nothing is left dangling.

Covers spec stories 51, 52, 53, 62, and 65 for former recipients.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner can revoke a share from the share panel; the recipient disappears from the list of shares
- [ ] Revoking the last share removes the "shared" mark from the task in "My tasks"
- [ ] After a revoke, the task is gone from the recipient's "Shared with me" on their next page load
- [ ] After a revoke, any action or reload by the recipient on a page for that task shows not-found, and nothing they submit changes the task
- [ ] Revoking one recipient does not affect other recipients of the same task
- [ ] When the owner deletes a shared task, it is gone from every recipient's "Shared with me" and its address shows not-found for them
- [ ] Only the owner can revoke
- [ ] The same email can be shared with again after a revoke

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Three independent browser sessions: A as `a@example.com`, B as `b@example.com`, C as `c@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`). As A create "Plan trip" and "Book hotel". Share "Plan trip" with B (view) and with C (view); share "Book hotel" with B (view).

1. As B, open "Plan trip" from "Shared with me" and leave the page open.
2. As A, in the share panel of "Plan trip", revoke the share for `b@example.com`.
3. As B, reload the open "Plan trip" page.
4. As B, open "Shared with me". As C, open "Shared with me".
5. As B, open "Book hotel" and leave the page open.
6. As A, delete "Book hotel" and confirm.
7. As B, reload the open page, then open "Shared with me".
8. As A, revoke the share for `c@example.com` on "Plan trip", then look at "My tasks".

**Expected:** after step 2 the share panel lists only `c@example.com`. Step 3 shows the not-found page. In step 4 B's list no longer contains "Plan trip" (it still contains "Book hotel"); C's list still contains "Plan trip". Step 7 shows the not-found page, and B's "Shared with me" shows its empty state. After step 8 "Plan trip" is no longer marked as shared. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the expected not-found responses.

**Edge case:** as A, share "Plan trip" with `b@example.com` again with the view role: it succeeds and B sees the task in "Shared with me" again. B is never offered a control to revoke or manage shares.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.6 Delete a task with confirmation
- task-master-42j.11 Share a task with the view role and "Shared with me"
close_reason: revoke share and delete cascade done

title: Edit role, replacing a role, and server-side refusal
description:
## What to build

The edit role becomes real. A recipient with the edit role can change a shared task's title, status, priority, due date and recurrence, under the same rules as the owner (title validation, completion moment set and cleared by status moves). They still cannot delete the task or manage its shares. The owner sees the recipient's changes the next time they load the task.

Sharing a task again with the same recipient replaces that recipient's role: there is at most one share per task and recipient, and changing a role is the same action as sharing.

Roles are enforced by the server on every request, not just by hiding controls. A recipient whose role no longer allows a change is refused and the task is left unchanged, even if they submit from a page they opened while they still had the edit role.

Task access now answers owner, edit, view or none, and every mutation goes through it.

Covers spec stories 47, 59, 60, 64.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An edit recipient sees edit and status controls on a shared task, including "mark done" in "Shared with me"
- [ ] An edit recipient can change title, status, priority, due date and recurrence
- [ ] The owner sees those changes on their next page load
- [ ] An edit recipient is not offered, and cannot perform, delete or share management
- [ ] Sharing again with the same recipient replaces the role; the share panel still lists that recipient once
- [ ] The recipient's "Shared with me" shows the new role on their next page load
- [ ] A change submitted by a recipient whose role is view is refused with a message and the task is unchanged, including from a stale page opened under the edit role
- [ ] Marking a shared task done as an edit recipient sets the completion moment exactly as for the owner

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database, clock set to 2030-02-01 09:00 UTC. Two independent browser sessions: A registered as `a@example.com`, B as `b@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`). As A create "Plan trip" and share it with `b@example.com` with the view role.

1. As A, in the share panel of "Plan trip", share with `b@example.com` again choosing the edit role.
2. As B, reload "Shared with me" and open "Plan trip".
3. As B, change the title to "Plan summer trip", priority to high, due date to 2030-06-01, recurrence to weekly and status to done; save.
4. As A, reload "Plan trip".
5. As B, open the edit form of "Plan summer trip" and leave it open without saving.
6. As A, share with `b@example.com` again choosing the view role.
7. As B, in the still-open form change the title to "Hijacked" and save.
8. As A and as B, reload the task.

**Expected:** after step 1 the share panel lists `b@example.com` exactly once, with role edit. In step 2 B's role shows edit and edit controls are offered, but no delete or share controls. After step 4 A sees "Plan summer trip", priority high, due 1 June 2030, recurrence weekly, status done, completed 1 February 2030. After step 6 the panel lists `b@example.com` once with role view. In step 7 the save is refused with a message that B is not allowed to change the task. After step 8 both see the title "Plan summer trip", and B sees role view with no edit controls. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the refused save in step 7.

**Edge case:** while B has the edit role, B clears the title and saves: the same "title is required" message the owner would get is shown and the title is unchanged.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.7 Status moves and completion moment
- task-master-42j.11 Share a task with the view role and "Shared with me"
close_reason: edit role and server-side refusal done

title: Share a task with the view role and "Shared with me"
description:
## What to build

An owner shares a task with another user by entering that user's email and choosing a role. This ticket makes the view role work end to end; the role choice already offers view and edit, but edit behaves as view until the follow-up ticket.

On the owner's side, the task detail view has a share management panel: a form to share (email plus role) and a list of every share on the task showing the recipient's email and role. "My tasks" shows at a glance which tasks are shared. The recipient must be a registered user (email matched after trimming and lower-casing); an unknown email is reported as an error, and an owner cannot share a task with themselves. Only the owner can share or see the list of shares.

On the recipient's side, a "Shared with me" list, separate from "My tasks", shows the tasks shared with them, each with the owner's email and the recipient's role. Opening a shared task shows all its fields. A recipient with the view role gets no edit controls, and no recipient is offered delete or share controls or sees the task's other recipients. Shared tasks never appear in the recipient's "My tasks".

Task access now answers owner, view or none (edit arrives next), and every read still goes through it.

Covers spec stories 45, 46, 48, 49, 50, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 61.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner can share a task by entering a registered user's email and choosing a role
- [ ] The task's share panel lists each share with recipient email and role
- [ ] "My tasks" visibly marks tasks that have at least one share
- [ ] Sharing with an email that is not a registered user shows an error and creates no share
- [ ] Sharing a task with the owner's own email shows an error and creates no share
- [ ] The recipient sees the task in "Shared with me", with the owner's email and their own role, and not in "My tasks"
- [ ] A view recipient can open the task and see title, status, priority, due date and recurrence, with no edit, status, delete or share controls
- [ ] A recipient cannot see the task's other recipients
- [ ] "Shared with me" has an empty state when nothing is shared with the user
- [ ] A user the task is not shared with still gets not-found for its address

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Use two independent browser sessions. In session A register `a@example.com`; in session B register `b@example.com`; in a third session register `c@example.com` (all with password `correct-horse-1`). As A create "Plan trip" with priority high and due date 2030-05-01, and a second task "Private note".

1. As B, open "Shared with me".
2. As A, open "Plan trip", and in the share panel enter ` B@Example.com `, choose the view role and share.
3. As A, share "Plan trip" with `c@example.com` with the view role, then go to "My tasks".
4. As B, reload "Shared with me", then check "My tasks".
5. As B, open "Plan trip" from "Shared with me".
6. As B, try opening the address of A's "Private note".

**Expected:** step 1 shows an empty state. After step 2 the share panel lists `b@example.com` with role view. After step 3 the panel lists both recipients, and "My tasks" marks "Plan trip" as shared while "Private note" is not marked. In step 4 "Shared with me" lists "Plan trip" with owner `a@example.com` and role view; B's "My tasks" does not contain it. In step 5 B sees title, status todo, priority high, due 1 May 2030 and recurrence, with no controls to edit, change status, delete or share, and no mention of `c@example.com`. Step 6 shows the not-found page. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the expected not-found.

**Edge case:** as A, in the share panel of "Plan trip" share with `nobody@example.com`: an error says no user has that email and the list is unchanged. Share with `a@example.com`: an error says you cannot share a task with yourself and the list is unchanged.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.3 Sign in, sign out and the signed-out redirect
- task-master-42j.5 Task detail: edit title, priority, due date and recurrence
close_reason: share with view role and Shared with me done

title: Archived tasks: hidden, opt-in, read-only, owner can delete
description:
## What to build

A task that was completed more than 30 days ago is an archived task. Archived tasks disappear from the default "My tasks" list. The user can turn on "show archived" to see them; they are then visibly marked "Archived". An archived task is read-only: no field, including status, can be changed, so it can never be restored. Its owner can still delete it.

Archived is derived from the completion moment and the clock on every request, never stored; there is no background job and no archive action. A task completed exactly 30 days ago or less stays in the normal list. The "show archived" choice lives in the page address like the other list options.

Covers spec stories 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A task completed more than 30 days before now is hidden from the default "My tasks" list
- [ ] A task completed exactly 30 days ago, or more recently, stays in the default list and remains editable
- [ ] Turning on "show archived" lists archived tasks, each marked "Archived"
- [ ] "Show archived" survives a reload
- [ ] An archived task's detail view shows all its fields with no edit or status controls
- [ ] The server rejects any change to an archived task, even from a page opened before it became archived, and the task is left unchanged
- [ ] The owner can delete an archived task, with the usual confirmation
- [ ] Reopening and re-completing a task before it is archived restarts the 30-day count from the new completion moment

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`). Set the clock to 2030-01-01 10:00:00 UTC, create "Old report" and mark it done. Set the clock to 2030-01-01 10:00:01 UTC, create "Boundary report" and mark it done. Create "Open task" and leave it todo.

1. Set the clock to 2030-01-31 10:00:01 UTC and reload "My tasks". ("Old report" was completed 30 days and 1 second ago; "Boundary report" exactly 30 days ago.)
2. Turn on "show archived", then reload.
3. Open "Old report".
4. Open "Boundary report" in a second tab and leave its edit form open without saving. Set the clock to 2030-01-31 10:00:02 UTC. In that stale tab change the title to "Changed" and save.
5. Back in "My tasks" with "show archived" on, delete "Old report" and confirm.

**Expected:** after step 1 "Boundary report" and "Open task" are listed and "Old report" is not. After step 2 all three are listed and "Old report" is marked "Archived", before and after the reload. In step 3 all fields of "Old report" are shown and there are no controls to edit fields or change status. In step 4 the save is refused with a message that archived tasks cannot be changed, and after reload the title is still "Boundary report", now marked "Archived". After step 5 "Old report" is gone from the list with "show archived" on. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the refused save in step 4.

**Edge case:** set the clock to 2030-03-01 10:00 UTC, create "Redo", mark it done, set the clock to 2030-03-20 10:00 UTC, change its status to todo and then done again. Set the clock to 2030-04-10 10:00 UTC (40 days after the first completion, 21 after the second): "Redo" is still in the default list and not marked "Archived".

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.5 Task detail: edit title, priority, due date and recurrence
- task-master-42j.6 Delete a task with confirmation
- task-master-42j.7 Status moves and completion moment

title: Overdue marking and overdue-only filter
description:
## What to build

A task whose due date is before today and whose status is not done is clearly marked "Overdue" in "My tasks" and in its detail view. A task due today is not overdue. A done task is never overdue, however old its due date. The mark always reflects the current facts: it goes away as soon as the task is completed or its due date is moved to today or later. Overdue is derived from the clock on every view, never stored. "Today" is the current calendar day in the application-wide time zone.

"My tasks" also gains an "overdue only" filter that lives in the page address alongside the other filters.

Covers spec stories 33, 34, 35, 36, 37.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A not-done task with a due date before today is marked "Overdue"
- [ ] A task due today is not marked overdue
- [ ] A task due in the future, or with no due date, is not marked overdue
- [ ] A done task is never marked overdue
- [ ] Completing an overdue task removes the mark
- [ ] Moving an overdue task's due date to today or later removes the mark
- [ ] An "overdue only" filter shows just the overdue tasks, combines with the other filters, and survives a reload
- [ ] The mark follows the clock: a task not overdue today becomes overdue when the clock passes into the day after its due date

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Set the clock to 2030-03-10 12:00 UTC (see README for the test-only clock control). Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and create these tasks through the UI:

| Title | Status | Due date |
|---|---|---|
| Yesterday | todo | 2030-03-09 |
| Today | todo | 2030-03-10 |
| Tomorrow | doing | 2030-03-11 |
| Old and done | done | 2030-01-01 |
| No date | todo | none |

1. Look at "My tasks".
2. Turn on the "overdue only" filter, then reload.
3. Turn the filter off. Set the clock to 2030-03-11 00:30 UTC and reload.
4. Mark "Yesterday" done.
5. Open "Today" and change its due date to 2030-03-11.

**Expected:** in step 1 only "Yesterday" is marked "Overdue". After step 2 only "Yesterday" is listed, before and after the reload. After step 3 "Yesterday" and "Today" are marked overdue; "Tomorrow" (now due today) is not. After step 4 "Yesterday" is no longer marked. After step 5 "Today" is no longer marked. "Old and done" and "No date" are never marked at any point. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** reopen "Old and done" by changing its status to todo: it becomes marked "Overdue" immediately; mark it done again and the mark disappears.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.8 Filter and sort "My tasks" in the page address

title: Filter and sort "My tasks" in the page address
description:
## What to build

A user narrows and orders "My tasks": filter by status, filter by priority, and sort by due date (tasks without a due date last) or by priority (high first). The filter and sort state lives in the page address, so it survives a reload and can be bookmarked.

Covers spec stories 28, 29, 30, 31.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "My tasks" can be filtered by status (todo, doing, done)
- [ ] "My tasks" can be filtered by priority (low, medium, high)
- [ ] Status and priority filters combine
- [ ] Sorting by due date puts the earliest due date first and tasks without a due date last
- [ ] Sorting by priority puts high first, then medium, then low
- [ ] The chosen filters and sort are part of the page address and are restored on reload or when the address is opened in a new tab
- [ ] When filters match nothing, a message says no tasks match (distinct from the "no tasks yet" empty state) and offers a way to clear the filters

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and create these five tasks, setting fields through the UI:

| Title | Status | Priority | Due date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alpha | todo | high | 2030-03-20 |
| Bravo | todo | high | 2030-03-05 |
| Charlie | todo | high | none |
| Delta | doing | low | 2030-03-01 |
| Echo | done | medium | 2030-03-10 |

1. On "My tasks", filter status to todo.
2. Additionally filter priority to high and sort by due date.
3. Reload the page.
4. Copy the page address and open it in a new tab.
5. Clear all filters and sort by priority.

**Expected:** after step 1 only Alpha, Bravo, Charlie are listed. After step 2 the order is Bravo, Alpha, Charlie. Steps 3 and 4 show the same three tasks in the same order with the filter and sort controls showing the chosen values. After step 5 all five tasks are listed with Alpha, Bravo, Charlie (high) first, then Echo (medium), then Delta (low). Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** filter status to done and priority to high: no tasks are listed, a "no tasks match" message is shown rather than the first-task empty state, and clearing the filters brings all five back.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.5 Task detail: edit title, priority, due date and recurrence
- task-master-42j.7 Status moves and completion moment
close_reason: filter and sort via URL done

title: Status moves and completion moment
description:
## What to build

A user moves a task between the statuses todo, doing and done in any direction, and can mark a task done with one action straight from "My tasks".

When a task's status becomes done it is completed: it carries the moment it became done, taken from the clock, and shows it. When its status leaves done the completion moment is cleared. Completing it again sets a fresh completion moment. Changing other fields of a done task leaves its completion moment untouched.

Covers spec stories 21, 22, 23, 24, 25.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A task's status can be changed from any of todo, doing, done to any other
- [ ] "My tasks" offers a one-action "mark done" control per task that is not done
- [ ] A completed task shows when it was completed, in "My tasks" and wherever else the task is shown
- [ ] The completion moment comes from the clock
- [ ] Moving a task out of done removes the completion moment
- [ ] Completing a reopened task shows the new completion moment, not the old one
- [ ] Changing another field of a completed task does not change its completion moment

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Using the test-only clock control (see README), set the clock to 2030-01-10 09:00 UTC. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and create a task "Buy milk".

1. On "My tasks", use the one-action "mark done" control on "Buy milk".
2. Change the status of "Buy milk" to doing.
3. Change the status to todo, then back to doing, then to done, setting the clock to 2030-01-12 09:00 UTC just before the final change.
4. Set the clock to 2030-01-14 09:00 UTC, then change any other editable field of the task (for example its title to "Buy oat milk").
5. Reload the page.

**Expected:** after step 1 the task shows status done and "completed" on 10 January 2030. After step 2 the status is doing and no completion date is shown. After step 3 the status is done and the completion date is 12 January 2030. After steps 4 and 5 the completion date is still 12 January 2030. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** every one of the six moves (todo to doing, todo to done, doing to todo, doing to done, done to todo, done to doing) is accepted, and a task that is todo or doing never shows a completion date.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.4 Create a task and see it in "My tasks"
close_reason: status moves and completion moment done

title: Delete a task with confirmation
description:
## What to build

An owner deletes a task. Before anything is removed the owner must confirm, so a misclick does not lose a task. A deleted task disappears from "My tasks" and its address shows not-found.

Covers spec stories 19, 20.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner is offered a "Delete" control for their task
- [ ] Choosing delete asks for confirmation naming the task
- [ ] Cancelling the confirmation leaves the task untouched
- [ ] Confirming removes the task from "My tasks"
- [ ] The deleted task's address shows the not-found page
- [ ] Only the owner can delete; the server refuses a delete from anyone else

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and create two tasks, "Buy milk" and "Call plumber". Note the page address of "Buy milk" if it has its own page.

1. Choose "Delete" for "Buy milk".
2. In the confirmation, choose "Cancel".
3. Choose "Delete" for "Buy milk" again and confirm.
4. Reload "My tasks".
5. Open the address of the deleted task.

**Expected:** after step 2 both tasks are still listed. After steps 3 and 4 only "Call plumber" is listed. Step 5 shows the not-found page. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the expected not-found response.

**Edge case:** in a second browser session register `b@example.com` and open the address of user A's "Call plumber": the not-found page is shown and no delete control is offered; user A still sees "Call plumber" afterwards.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.4 Create a task and see it in "My tasks"

title: Create a task and see it in "My tasks"
description:
## What to build

A user creates a task by typing just a title on "My tasks" and immediately sees it in their list. A new task starts with status todo, priority medium, no due date and recurrence none, and belongs to the user who created it (its owner). "My tasks" lists only the tasks the user owns; a user never sees another user's task. With no tasks, the page shows an empty state that tells the user how to add their first task.

This ticket introduces task access, the single place that answers "what may this user do with this task?". Here it only needs to distinguish owner from none; every read of a task goes through it.

Covers spec stories 10, 11, 12, 26, 27, 32.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can create a task by entering only a title
- [ ] The new task appears in "My tasks" without a manual reload, showing status todo and priority medium
- [ ] The title is trimmed; an empty or whitespace-only title is rejected with a message and no task is created
- [ ] A title longer than 200 characters is rejected with a message
- [ ] "My tasks" shows only tasks owned by the signed-in user
- [ ] With no tasks, an empty state explains how to create the first task

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`); you are on "My tasks".

1. Confirm the empty state is shown.
2. Type `  Buy milk  ` into the new task title field and submit.
3. Reload the page.
4. In a second, separate browser session register `b@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and look at "My tasks".

**Expected:** step 1 shows an empty state with guidance on adding a task. After step 2 a task titled exactly "Buy milk" is listed with status todo and priority medium, and the empty state is gone. After step 3 it is still listed. In step 4 user B sees the empty state and no "Buy milk". Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** as user A, submit the new task field containing only spaces: a message says a title is required and the list still has exactly one task. Submit a title of 201 characters: a message says the title is too long and no task is added.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.2 Register an account

title: Task detail: edit title, priority, due date and recurrence
description:
## What to build

An owner opens a task from "My tasks" into a task detail view and changes its title, priority (low, medium, high), due date and recurrence (none, daily, weekly). The due date is a calendar day with no time; it can be set and cleared. Recurrence is stored and editable only; it causes no behaviour. "My tasks" shows each task's priority and due date.

A user with no access to a task sees the same not-found page as for a task that does not exist, so a task's existence is not leaked by its address.

Covers spec stories 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 65 for users with no access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a task in "My tasks" opens its detail view showing title, status, priority, due date and recurrence
- [ ] The owner can rename the task; the same title rules apply as on creation (trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 characters)
- [ ] The owner can set priority to low, medium or high
- [ ] The owner can set a due date as a calendar day and clear it again
- [ ] The owner can set recurrence to none, daily or weekly; nothing repeats as a result
- [ ] Changes persist across a reload and are reflected in "My tasks"
- [ ] The due date shown is the same calendar day that was entered, whatever the application time zone
- [ ] Opening the address of another user's task, or of a task that does not exist, shows the same not-found page

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` (password `correct-horse-1`) and create a task "Buy milk".

1. Open "Buy milk" from "My tasks".
2. Change the title to "Buy oat milk", priority to high, due date to 2030-03-10 and recurrence to weekly; save.
3. Reload the page, then go back to "My tasks".
4. Open the task again, clear the due date and save; reload.
5. Copy the task's page address. In a second browser session register `b@example.com` and open that address.
6. As user B, open the address of a task that cannot exist (change the id in the address to a made-up value).

**Expected:** after step 3 the detail view and "My tasks" both show "Buy oat milk", priority high, due 10 March 2030; the detail view shows recurrence weekly. After step 4 the task has no due date. Steps 5 and 6 show the identical not-found page with no task details. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests other than the expected not-found responses.

**Edge case:** as user A, clear the title entirely and save: a message says a title is required and the title remains "Buy oat milk" after reload. Enter a 201-character title and save: a message says the title is too long and the title is unchanged.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.4 Create a task and see it in "My tasks"

title: Sign in, sign out and the signed-out redirect
description:
## What to build

A registered user signs in with their email and password, and signs out again. A failed sign-in says only that the credentials are wrong, with the identical message whether the email is unknown or the password is wrong. A visitor who opens any task page without being signed in is sent to the sign-in page.

Covers spec stories 4, 5, 7, 8.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can sign in with their email and password and reaches "My tasks"
- [ ] The email is matched after trimming and lower-casing
- [ ] A signed-in user can sign out and is then treated as a visitor
- [ ] A wrong password and an unknown email produce exactly the same message
- [ ] Opening "My tasks" (or any task page) while signed out redirects to the sign-in page
- [ ] After signing out, the browser's back button does not reveal task pages

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database. Register `a@example.com` with password `correct-horse-1` through the registration page (this leaves you signed in).

1. Use the "Sign out" control.
2. Open the "My tasks" page address directly.
3. On the sign-in page enter `a@example.com` and `correct-horse-1`, then submit.

**Expected:** after step 1 the sign-in page (or a signed-out landing page) is shown and the email is no longer displayed. After step 2 the sign-in page is shown, not the task list. After step 3 "My tasks" is shown with `a@example.com` visible. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** sign out again, then on the sign-in page try `a@example.com` with `wrong-password-1`, and then `nobody@example.com` with `correct-horse-1`. Both attempts stay on the sign-in page and show word-for-word the same message that the credentials are wrong; neither says whether the email exists.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.2 Register an account
close_reason: sign in/out and signed-out redirect done

title: Register an account
description:
## What to build

A visitor registers as a user with an email and a password and lands signed in on their own, empty "My tasks" page, which shows the email they are signed in as. They stay signed in across page reloads and browser restarts.

Emails are normalised (trimmed, lower-cased) before the uniqueness check. Passwords are stored only as a salted hash from a standard password-hashing algorithm. Sessions are stored server-side and referenced by an http-only cookie that outlives the browser session. Minimum password length is 8 characters.

Covers spec stories 1, 2, 3, 6, 9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can register with a valid email and a password of at least 8 characters
- [ ] After registering, the user is signed in and sees the "My tasks" page
- [ ] The signed-in user's email is visible on the page
- [ ] The user is still signed in after a reload and after closing and reopening the browser
- [ ] Registering an email already in use shows a message saying the email is already registered, compared after trimming and lower-casing
- [ ] A malformed email shows a validation message
- [ ] A password shorter than 8 characters shows a validation message
- [ ] The password is never stored in plain text

## Verification steps

**Preconditions:** application running in test mode on an empty database; nobody signed in. Open the registration page.

1. Enter email `a@example.com` and password `correct-horse-1`, then submit.
2. Reload the page.
3. Close the browser, reopen it and open the application again.

**Expected:** after step 1 the "My tasks" heading is shown and `a@example.com` is visible as the signed-in user. After steps 2 and 3 the same page is shown, still signed in. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** in a second, signed-out browser session open the registration page and try, one at a time:
- email ` A@Example.com ` (different case, surrounding spaces) with password `correct-horse-1`: a message says the email is already registered; no new user is signed in.
- email `not-an-email` with password `correct-horse-1`: a validation message about the email is shown.
- email `c@example.com` with password `short`: a validation message about the password length is shown.

## Blocked by

- task-master-42j.1 Walking skeleton with browser test harness, clock and database controls
close_reason: registration with scrypt hashing and server-side sessions done

title: Walking skeleton with browser test harness, clock and database controls
description:
## What to build

Stand up the Task Manager as a single Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) application backed by SQLite with versioned migrations, plus the browser test harness every later ticket is delivered against.

The application has a clock: the only source of "now" and "today". "Today" is the current calendar day in one application-wide time zone taken from configuration, UTC by default. The home page shows today's date from the clock, which is enough to prove the whole path (browser, server, clock) works.

Two test-only controls exist when the application runs in test mode: set the clock to a chosen moment, and start from an empty database. Neither exists in a production build. Each browser test gets its own isolated SQLite database so tests can run in parallel and in any order. Tests locate elements by accessible role and label only.

The README documents: how to install, how to run the application, how to run it in test mode, how to use the two test-only controls by hand, and the command that runs the browser tests. Later tickets' verification steps rely on this documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The application starts locally and the home page shows today's date taken from the clock
- [ ] Database schema is created by versioned migrations applied automatically on a fresh database
- [ ] In test mode the clock can be set to a chosen moment and the home page reflects it
- [ ] In test mode the database can be reset to empty
- [ ] Neither test-only control is reachable in a production build
- [ ] Browser tests run with one command, each test on its own isolated database, in parallel
- [ ] The application-wide time zone comes from configuration and defaults to UTC
- [ ] The README documents run, test mode, the two controls and the test command

## Verification steps

UI: none (harness ticket). Command-level checks:

**Preconditions:** fresh clone, dependencies installed as the README describes.

1. Run the browser test command from the README.
2. Start the application in test mode as the README describes and open the home page.
3. Use the test-only clock control to set the clock to 2030-01-15 10:00 UTC, then reload the home page.
4. Use the test-only database control to reset to an empty database.
5. Build and start the application in production mode, then try both test-only controls the same way.

**Expected:** step 1 exits successfully and includes at least one test that sets the clock and asserts the date shown on the home page changes. After step 3 the home page shows 15 January 2030. Step 4 succeeds. Browser console clean; no unexpected failed requests.

**Edge case:** in step 5 both test-only controls are unavailable (not found), and the home page shows the real current date.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
close_reason: skeleton, clock, test controls, playwright harness done

title: Spec: Task Manager — accounts, tasks, overdue, archived tasks, and sharing with roles
description:
## Problem Statement

People who keep a to-do list usually keep it alone, and the moment a task involves someone else it leaves the list: it gets pasted into a chat, re-typed into someone else's notes, and the two copies drift apart. There is no place where a user can keep their own tasks private by default and still hand a single task to another user, deciding whether that person may only look at it or may also change it.

Alongside that, a personal task list becomes noisy over time. Tasks that slipped past their due date are not obvious, and tasks completed long ago keep cluttering the list.

The repository currently contains only the domain glossary; there is no application.

## Solution

Build the Task Manager: a multi-user web application where each user signs in with their email, keeps their own tasks, and can share individual tasks with other users.

A user creates tasks with a title, a status (todo, doing, done), a priority (low, medium, high), an optional due date and a recurrence setting. Overdue tasks are flagged. Tasks completed more than 30 days ago become archived tasks: hidden by default, read-only, and removable only by their owner.

The owner of a task can share it with another user by email, choosing a role of view or edit, change that role later by sharing again, and revoke the share. Recipients see shared tasks in their own "Shared with me" list and can act on them exactly as far as their role allows.

## User Stories

### Accounts

1. As a visitor, I want to register with my email and a password, so that I have my own private task list.
2. As a visitor, I want to be told when the email I am registering is already in use, so that I know to sign in instead.
3. As a visitor, I want clear validation messages for a malformed email or a too-short password, so that I can fix my input.
4. As a user, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can reach my tasks.
5. As a user, I want a failed sign-in to say only that the credentials are wrong, so that nobody can probe which emails are registered through the sign-in form.
6. As a user, I want to stay signed in across page reloads and browser restarts, so that I do not have to sign in every visit.
7. As a user, I want to sign out, so that nobody else using my device can reach my tasks.
8. As a visitor, I want to be sent to the sign-in page when I open any task page without being signed in, so that tasks are never exposed anonymously.
9. As a user, I want to see which email I am signed in as, so that I know whose tasks I am looking at.

### Creating and editing tasks

10. As a user, I want to create a task by typing just a title, so that capturing a task is fast.
11. As a user, I want a new task to start with status todo and priority medium, so that I only set those when they differ from the usual.
12. As a user, I want to be stopped from creating a task with an empty or whitespace-only title, so that my list has no blank entries.
13. As a user, I want to set a priority of low, medium or high on a task, so that I can tell what matters most.
14. As a user, I want to set a due date as a calendar day, so that I know which day a task should be completed by.
15. As a user, I want to clear a due date, so that a task can go back to having no due date.
16. As a user, I want to set a recurrence of none, daily or weekly on a task, so that the setting is recorded for when repetition rules are decided.
17. As an owner, I want to rename a task, so that I can correct or refine it.
18. As an owner, I want to change priority, due date and recurrence after creating a task, so that the task keeps up with reality.
19. As an owner, I want to delete a task, so that I can remove things I no longer care about.
20. As an owner, I want to confirm before a task is deleted, so that I do not lose a task by a misclick.

### Status and completion

21. As a user, I want to move a task between todo, doing and done in any direction, so that I am never trapped by a fixed workflow.
22. As a user, I want to mark a task done with one action from the list, so that completing work is quick.
23. As a user, I want a completed task to show when it was completed, so that I can see when work was finished.
24. As a user, I want a task that leaves done to lose its completion moment, so that reopening it does not leave a stale completion record.
25. As a user, I want a reopened and re-completed task to carry the new completion moment, so that the 30-day archive countdown starts again.

### Viewing my tasks

26. As a user, I want a "My tasks" list of the tasks I own, so that I can see my own work in one place.
27. As a user, I want never to see another user's task unless it has been shared with me, so that task lists are private by default.
28. As a user, I want to filter my list by status, so that I can focus on what is still open.
29. As a user, I want to filter my list by priority, so that I can focus on what is important.
30. As a user, I want to sort my list by due date or priority, so that I can decide what to do next.
31. As a user, I want my filters to survive a page reload, so that I do not have to reapply them.
32. As a user, I want a useful empty state when I have no tasks, so that I know how to start.

### Overdue

33. As a user, I want a task whose due date is before today and that is not done to be clearly marked overdue, so that slipped work stands out.
34. As a user, I want a task due today not to be marked overdue, so that I am not nagged about work that is still on time.
35. As a user, I want a done task never to be marked overdue, however old its due date, so that finished work is not flagged.
36. As a user, I want to filter to only overdue tasks, so that I can catch up on what slipped.
37. As a user, I want an overdue task to stop being overdue as soon as I complete it or move its due date to today or later, so that the flag always reflects the current facts.

### Archived tasks

38. As a user, I want tasks completed more than 30 days ago to disappear from my default list, so that old finished work does not clutter it.
39. As a user, I want to opt in to seeing archived tasks, so that I can still look up old work.
40. As a user, I want archived tasks to be visibly marked as archived, so that I understand why I cannot change them.
41. As a user, I want archived tasks to be read-only, so that the historical record cannot be altered.
42. As an owner, I want to delete an archived task, so that I can clear out history I do not need.
43. As a user, I want a task completed exactly 30 days ago or less to stay in my normal list, so that recently finished work stays visible.
44. As a recipient, I want an archived task that was shared with me to remain visible in my archived view, read-only whatever my role, so that I can still look it up.

### Sharing

45. As an owner, I want to share a task with another user by entering their email, so that they can see it.
46. As an owner, I want to choose a role of view or edit when I share, so that I control what the recipient may do.
47. As an owner, I want sharing a task again with the same recipient to replace their role, so that changing a role is the same action as sharing.
48. As an owner, I want to be told when the email I entered does not belong to a registered user, so that I know the share did not happen.
49. As an owner, I want to be stopped from sharing a task with myself, so that there are no meaningless shares.
50. As an owner, I want to see every share on a task with the recipient's email and role, so that I know who has access.
51. As an owner, I want to revoke a share, so that the recipient loses access.
52. As an owner, I want a revoked recipient to lose access immediately, including on a page they already have open, so that revoking is trustworthy.
53. As an owner, I want deleting a task to remove it from every recipient's list, so that nothing is left dangling.
54. As an owner, I want to see at a glance which of my tasks are shared, so that I remember what others can see.

### Receiving shared tasks

55. As a recipient, I want a "Shared with me" list separate from my own tasks, so that I can tell my tasks from other users' tasks.
56. As a recipient, I want to see who owns each shared task, so that I know whose work it is.
57. As a recipient, I want to see my role on each shared task, so that I know what I am allowed to do.
58. As a recipient with the view role, I want to see all of a task's fields without any edit controls, so that I am not offered actions that will fail.
59. As a recipient with the edit role, I want to change the title, status, priority, due date and recurrence, so that I can genuinely work on the task.
60. As a recipient with the edit role, I want the owner to see my changes the next time they load the task, so that we share one source of truth.
61. As a recipient, I want not to be offered delete or share controls, so that it is clear those belong to the owner.
62. As a recipient, I want a task to vanish from my list once its share is revoked or the task is deleted, so that my list reflects my real access.
63. As a recipient, I want overdue marking and archiving to behave on shared tasks exactly as on my own, so that the rules are consistent.

### Safety

64. As a user, I want the server to refuse any change my role does not allow, even if I craft the request by hand, so that roles are real and not just hidden buttons.
65. As a user, I want a task I have no access to to look as if it does not exist, so that task existence is not leaked by its address.

## Implementation Decisions

### Stack

- Next.js with the App Router and TypeScript, as a single deployable application serving both the UI and the server-side logic.
- SQLite as the database, accessed through a typed query layer with versioned migrations.
- Pages render on the server from the signed-in user's data; mutations go through server actions. No separate public REST API is designed in this spec.

### Modules

- **Clock**: the only source of "now" and "today" in the application. Everything that depends on time (completion moment, overdue, archived) asks the clock. In test mode only, the clock can be set to a chosen moment; that control does not exist in a production build.
- **Accounts**: registration, sign-in, sign-out and the current-user lookup. Emails are normalised (trimmed, lower-cased) before the uniqueness check. Passwords are stored only as a salted hash from a standard password-hashing algorithm. Sessions are stored server-side and referenced by an http-only cookie.
- **Task access**: the single place that answers "what may this user do with this task?" It returns one of: owner, edit, view, or none. Every read and every mutation goes through it. This is the deep module that makes roles trustworthy; UI code hides controls based on its answer but never substitutes for it.
- **Tasks**: create, read, update, delete and list tasks, built on task access and the clock. Owns the derivation of completed, overdue and archived.
- **Shares**: share (create or replace role), list and revoke, owner-only.
- **Web UI**: sign-up and sign-in pages, "My tasks", "Shared with me", a task detail/edit view and the share management panel within it.

### Domain rules

- A task belongs to exactly one owner, set at creation and never changed.
- Title is required, trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 characters.
- Status is todo, doing or done; any status may move to any other. New tasks are todo.
- Priority is low, medium or high; medium by default.
- Due date is an optional calendar day stored as a date with no time and no time zone.
- Recurrence is none, daily or weekly, none by default. It is stored and editable only; it causes no behaviour.
- **Completed**: when status becomes done, the completion moment is set from the clock. When status leaves done, the completion moment is cleared. Editing other fields of a done task leaves the completion moment untouched.
- **Overdue** is derived, never stored: due date is before today and status is not done.
- **Archived task** is derived, never stored: the task is completed and its completion moment is more than 30 days before now. There is no background job and no archive action. Because an archived task is read-only its status cannot leave done, so it can never stop being archived, which satisfies "cannot be restored".
- "Today" is the current calendar day in a single application-wide time zone taken from configuration, UTC by default.
- An archived task rejects every mutation except deletion by its owner. That includes share and revoke: its shares are frozen until the task is deleted.
- Deleting a task deletes its shares.

### Sharing rules

- A share links one task to one recipient with a role of view or edit. There is at most one share per task and recipient, enforced by a uniqueness constraint; sharing again replaces the role.
- The recipient is identified by email and must be a registered user. An unknown email is reported to the owner as an error. An owner cannot share a task with themselves.
- Only the owner can share, revoke, list shares and delete the task.
- View role: read every field of the task. Edit role: additionally change title, status, priority, due date and recurrence.
- A recipient sees the owner's email on a shared task. Recipients do not see the other recipients of the task.
- Access is checked on every request, so revoking takes effect on the recipient's next request.
- A user with no access to a task receives the same not-found response as for a task that does not exist. A user with access but an insufficient role receives a forbidden response and the task is left unchanged.

### Schema

- **User**: id, email (unique), password hash, created moment.
- **Session**: id, user, expiry moment.
- **Task**: id, owner (user), title, status, priority, due date (nullable), recurrence, completion moment (nullable), created moment, updated moment.
- **Share**: task, recipient (user), role, created moment; unique on task and recipient; removed when its task is removed.

### Lists

- "My tasks" shows tasks the user owns. "Shared with me" shows tasks shared with the user. Both hide archived tasks unless the user turns on "show archived".
- Filters: status, priority, overdue only. Sorts: due date (tasks without a due date last) and priority (high first). Filter and sort state lives in the page address so it survives reloads and can be bookmarked.

## Testing Decisions

- **One seam: the browser.** Every test drives the running application through its real UI in a browser and asserts on what the user sees. This was chosen explicitly over an HTTP-level or service-level seam.
- A good test here describes behaviour in the glossary's terms and from a user's point of view: "a recipient with the view role cannot rename the task", not "the update action returns 403". It does not reach into the database, call server actions directly or assert on markup structure. Elements are located by accessible role and label, never by CSS class or generated id.
- Two test-only controls support the seam, neither of which is a second test surface for assertions: setting the clock, and starting each test from an empty database. Both must be unavailable in a production build. Everything else, including creating users and tasks, is done through the UI via shared helper steps.
- Each test gets its own isolated SQLite database so tests can run in parallel and in any order.
- Tests that involve two users (owner and recipient) use two independent browser sessions within one test.
- Time-dependent behaviour is tested by moving the clock, never by waiting: the overdue boundary (due yesterday, today, tomorrow), and the archive boundary (completed exactly 30 days ago versus just over 30 days ago).
- "The server refuses what the role does not allow" is tested at the browser seam by having a recipient keep a page open while the owner downgrades or revokes the share, then attempting the action from the stale page.
- Coverage targets: accounts (register, duplicate email, sign in, sign out, redirect when signed out); task lifecycle (create with defaults, edit each field, status moves in every direction, completion moment set and cleared, delete); overdue; archived (hidden by default, visible on opt-in, read-only, owner can delete); sharing (share, replace role, unknown email, self-share, revoke, delete cascades); recipient experience per role; no access looks like not found.
- Prior art: none. The repository has no tests yet, so this spec establishes the pattern. The first ticket should stand up the browser test harness with the clock and database controls before feature work, so every later ticket is delivered test-first at this seam.

## Out of Scope

- Recurrence behaviour. The setting is stored and editable, but nothing repeats; the glossary records the rules as undecided.
- Restoring an archived task, or archiving a task manually.
- Email of any kind: verification, password reset, share notifications.
- Changing email or password, and deleting an account.
- Sharing with people who are not registered users, sharing by link, and sharing a whole list at once.
- Transferring ownership of a task.
- Recipients removing themselves from a share.
- Live updates; a user sees another user's changes on their next page load.
- Per-user time zones.
- Task descriptions, comments, attachments, subtasks, tags, lists/projects and search.
- A public API, mobile apps and offline use.
- Third-party sign-in.

## Further Notes

- The domain glossary at the repository root is the source of vocabulary for code, UI copy and test names: user, owner, recipient, task, status, completed, priority, due date, overdue, archived task, recurrence, share, role, revoke. Avoid the synonyms it lists.
- There are no ADRs yet. Three decisions in this spec are good candidates for one each, since they were made here rather than taken from the glossary: archived is derived rather than stored; "today" uses a single application-wide time zone; an archived task's shares are frozen.
- The sharing form reveals whether an email is registered (story 48). This is accepted because sharing is only possible between registered users and the alternative is silent failure.
- Choosing the browser as the only seam makes the suite slower than a lower seam would. Keep it fast by isolating databases per test, moving the clock instead of waiting, and keeping UI setup in shared helper steps.
